subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
title: Reading: Intensive Reading (Factual Texts)
overview: A factual text gives true information about a topic. In this sub-strand you will read factual texts of about 320 words on hygiene and sanitation, answer questions about them, work out the meaning of new words, and learn good reading habits that help you understand and remember what you read.

lessons.title: Reading a factual text: Germs and clean hands
objectives: Read a factual text of about 320 words on hygiene.
Answer factual and inferential questions on the text.
Work out the meaning of new words from the text.
lessons.intro: Every day your hands touch doors, desks, balls, money and food. Can you see what they pick up? Read the text below to find out why washing your hands is one of the simplest ways to stay healthy.
lessons.notes:
### What is a factual text?
A factual text tells us true things about the world. It does not tell a made-up story. It often has a title, short paragraphs, and sometimes headings or a list of steps.

### Read the text
**Germs and Clean Hands**

Germs are tiny living things. They are so small that we cannot see them without a microscope. Some germs are harmless, but others cause diseases such as diarrhoea, cholera and colds.

Germs spread easily. When a person uses the toilet or latrine, germs from faeces can stay on their hands. If that person then touches food, a cup or another person's hand without washing, the germs move on. Flies also carry germs. A fly that lands on waste and then on uncovered food leaves germs behind.

The good news is that we can stop many germs. Washing hands with soap and clean water removes germs that plain water leaves behind. Soap loosens the dirt and oil on the skin, and rinsing carries the germs away.

To wash your hands well, wet them with clean running water. Rub soap on both hands. Scrub the palms, the backs of the hands, between the fingers and under the nails for about twenty seconds. Rinse well and dry your hands with a clean cloth or let them dry in the air. At school you can use a tap or a leaky tin that pours water slowly.

When should you wash your hands? Always wash them after using the toilet, before eating, before handling food, after touching rubbish and after playing outside. Wash them after blowing your nose or coughing into them.

Other simple habits also keep germs away. Cover food and drinking water. Boil or treat drinking water when you are not sure it is safe. Keep toilets and latrines clean and cover the hole of a pit latrine. Throw refuse in a bin or a rubbish pit.

Clean hands protect you, your family and your classmates. Hygiene is everyone's responsibility.

### Working out new words
If you meet a new word, read the sentences around it. For example, "Soap loosens the dirt... and rinsing carries the germs away" helps you guess that rinsing means washing off with water.

keyWords.meaning: tiny living things that can cause disease
an instrument that makes very small things look bigger
solid waste that passes out of the body

examples.problem: Factual question: Name two diseases caused by germs mentioned in the text.
examples.answer: Any two of diarrhoea, cholera and colds.

examples.problem: Inferential question: Why do you think the writer says hygiene is everyone's responsibility?
examples.answer: Because germs spread from one person to another, so if one person is careless others can get sick too.

activity.title: Read, find and act
materials: Copy of the text or a digital device with the text
Soap, water and a basin or leaky tin
steps: Read the text silently once, then read it again with a partner, taking turns paragraph by paragraph.
Underline three words you did not know and guess their meaning from the sentences around them.
Answer the practice questions in your exercise book.
In groups, role play the handwashing steps from the text while one learner reads them aloud.

practice.question: Why can't we see germs?
practice.answer: They are too small to see without a microscope.

practice.question: How do flies spread germs?
practice.answer: They land on waste and then on uncovered food, leaving germs behind.

practice.question: List four times when you should wash your hands.
practice.answer: Any four: after using the toilet, before eating, before handling food, after touching rubbish, after playing outside, after blowing your nose.

practice.question: What does the word scrub mean in the text?

summary: A factual text gives true information.
Germs spread through dirty hands, flies, food and water.
Washing hands with soap and clean water removes germs.

lessons.title: Good reading habits
objectives: Read at the right speed without pointing or murmuring.
Use steps that help you remember what you read.
Use an encyclopaedia or dictionary to find more information.
lessons.intro: Two learners read the same text. One reads every word slowly with a finger and forgets the beginning by the end. The other reads smoothly and can tell you the main points. The difference is their reading habits.
lessons.notes:
Reading habits are the ways we usually read. Good habits help us read faster and understand more.

### Before reading
- Sit upright in good light, with the book about 30 centimetres from your eyes.
- Look at the title, headings and pictures. Ask yourself: What will this text tell me?

### While reading
- Read in groups of words, not one word at a time. "Wash your hands / with soap / and clean water" is easier to understand than stopping at every word.
- Do not point at each word with your finger or a pencil, and do not move your lips when reading silently. These habits slow you down.
- Read at the right speed. Too fast and you miss facts; too slow and you lose the meaning. Slow down a little for difficult parts.
- If a word is new, guess its meaning from the sentence, then check it in a dictionary.

### After reading
- Say the main idea of each paragraph in your own words.
- Write down key facts as short notes.
- Answer questions, then go back to the text to check your answers.

### Finding more information
An encyclopaedia is a book or website with factual articles on many topics, arranged from A to Z. To learn more about cholera, look under the letter C. A dictionary gives the meaning and pronunciation of words. Both are useful when a factual text leaves you with questions.

### Why remember what we read?
We read factual texts to learn. If you remember that cholera spreads through dirty water and food, you will know to boil water and cover food. Reading carefully helps you make good choices.

keyWords.meaning: the usual way a person reads
a book or website with facts on many topics arranged in alphabetical order
the most important point of a paragraph or text

examples.problem: Split this sentence into word groups for smooth reading: Cover your food to keep flies away from it.
examples.answer: Cover your food / to keep flies away / from it.

examples.problem: Under which letter would you look in an encyclopaedia to read about sanitation?

activity.title: Reading habits check
materials: The text Germs and Clean Hands
Encyclopaedia or dictionary, or a digital device
steps: In pairs, one learner reads a paragraph silently while the partner watches for pointing or lip movement.
Swap roles and give each other one tip to improve.
Write the main idea of each paragraph in one sentence.
Look up cholera or diarrhoea in an encyclopaedia or dictionary and share one new fact with the class.
Watch a short video on handwashing if available and pick out two steps it shows.

practice.question: Name two bad reading habits that slow you down.
practice.answer: Pointing at words, moving your lips while reading silently (also reading word by word).

practice.question: What should you do before you start reading a text?
practice.answer: Look at the title, headings and pictures and think about what the text is about.

practice.question: How can you check the meaning of a new word after guessing it?
practice.answer: Look it up in a dictionary.

summary: Preview, read in word groups and review.
Avoid pointing and murmuring when reading silently.
Use an encyclopaedia or dictionary to learn more.

lessons.title: Why we read for information: Keeping toilets and latrines clean
objectives: Read a second factual text using good reading habits.
Explain why reading for information is important.
lessons.intro: A clean toilet protects the whole school. Read this factual text about sanitation and use the reading habits you learnt in the last lesson.
lessons.notes:
### Read the text
**A Clean Toilet for Everyone**

Sanitation means the safe handling of human waste and refuse. Toilets and latrines are important parts of sanitation because they keep faeces away from people, food and water.

A flush toilet uses water to carry waste away through pipes. After using it, press the handle or pull the chain so that the waste is flushed. If there is no running water, pour water from a bucket into the bowl.

A pit latrine is a deep hole covered with a floor called a slab. Waste falls into the pit. A latrine must be kept covered with a lid when not in use so that flies cannot get in and out. Flies that visit uncovered latrines can carry germs to our food.

Everyone can help keep toilets clean. Aim well so that the floor stays dry. Use toilet paper and put it in the toilet or the pit, not on the floor. Never throw stones, bottles or plastic into a toilet or latrine, because they block it. Wash your hands with soap and water as soon as you leave.

People on duty should sweep and scrub the floor, rinse it with water and wipe the door handles. Many schools use a disinfectant to kill germs. Drainage around the toilet should be clear so that dirty water does not collect.

Dirty toilets smell bad and spread infection. When they are clean, learners are safe and comfortable. A clean toilet is a sign of a caring school.

### Reading for information
Why did we read this text carefully? Because it tells us what to do. A learner who has read it knows how to use a latrine safely and why the lid matters. Reading for information:

- helps us understand how things work;
- teaches us how to protect our health;
- helps us answer questions in all subjects;
- lets us share correct facts with our family.

Reading for comprehension means reading until you truly understand, not just saying the words.

keyWords.meaning: a toilet built over a deep hole in the ground
the flat floor covering a pit latrine
the way water flows away from a place

examples.problem: Factual: Why should a pit latrine be covered?
examples.answer: So that flies cannot get in and out and carry germs to food.

examples.problem: Inferential: Why does the writer say a clean toilet is a sign of a caring school?
examples.answer: Because keeping it clean shows people care about each other's health and comfort.

activity.title: Toilet duty role play
materials: The text A Clean Toilet for Everyone
steps: Read the text silently, then answer the practice questions.
In groups, role play a toilet duty team explaining to younger learners how to use and keep the latrine clean.
Discuss in your group: How did reading this text help you? Share your answer with the class.

practice.question: How does a flush toilet remove waste?
practice.answer: It uses water to carry waste away through pipes.

practice.question: Name two things that should never be thrown into a toilet.
What does drainage mean in the text?
practice.answer: The way dirty water flows away so that it does not collect.

practice.question: Give one reason why reading for information is important.
practice.answer: It teaches us how to protect our health (or helps us understand how things work, answer questions, share correct facts).

summary: Toilets and latrines keep faeces away from people, food and water.
Keep latrines covered and toilets clean and dry.
Reading for information helps us understand and act wisely.

quiz.question: What is a factual text?
options: A text that gives true information

quiz.question: According to Germs and Clean Hands, what removes germs that plain water leaves behind?
quiz.explanation: The text says soap and clean water remove germs.

quiz.question: For about how long should you scrub your hands?
quiz.explanation: The text says about twenty seconds.

quiz.question: In A Clean Toilet for Everyone, what is the floor that covers a pit latrine called?
quiz.explanation: The text calls it a slab.

quiz.question: Why should we not throw plastic into a latrine?
quiz.answer: It blocks the toilet or latrine.
quiz.explanation: The text says stones, bottles and plastic block it.

quiz.question: Which is a good reading habit?
options: Moving your lips when reading silently
quiz.explanation: Reading in word groups is faster and helps understanding.

quiz.question: What should you do after reading a text to remember it?
options: Close the book and forget it
Say the main ideas in your own words

quiz.question: Where would you look to find more facts about cholera?
quiz.explanation: An encyclopaedia has factual articles on many topics.

quiz.question: Why is it important to read for comprehension?
quiz.answer: So that we truly understand the information and can use it, for example to protect our health.
quiz.explanation: Understanding helps us act on what we read.

quiz.question: Which is NOT a reason for reading factual texts?
quiz.explanation: Factual texts are for true information, not made-up stories.
